text:
Credit marks climb toward the public rally

Rating: overweight

Private credit spent March 15, 2028 catching up rather than cracking. The reported_vs_public_gap of -8.5% simply reflects marks that update slower than public prices, not hidden deterioration. With hy_spread_now_bps at 380bps and drawdown flat at +0.0%, the underlying carry story remains intact: a one_year_return of +9.3% shows the asset class compounding through a policy_rate_now of 4.75% and cpi_now at 2.7%. Growth-supportive conditions continue to give borrowers room to refinance, and spread compression from here would only extend the constructive path already visible in the twelve-month number.

The newsflow that "public rally leaves private marks behind" is not evidence of fragility—it is evidence of a lag that markets have seen before. When listed comps rerate sharply, private valuations typically follow with delay, not with denial. The ytd_return of +1.0% looks modest against that backdrop, but it is consistent with a marking process that smooths rather than mispriced. Grimshaw Partners frames this lag as fragility compounding beneath stable marks; we read the same gap as convergence still in progress. Policy support and resilient growth conditions argue for marks catching up to fundamentals, not fundamentals catching down to marks.
